name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret. It cuts noise in PRs by fixing trivial formatting in upstream code, letting humans focus on real changes. The trade-off is trusting Pret’s safety checks—we accept the risk of rare misfires to save time.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "whitespace-only"—it’s that third-party dependencies of PR-Agent’s 90% threshold still ignores *what* the tool flags—it could block meaningful fixes while letting trivial formatting through. A better alternative: auto-apply only to our own codebase where we control the tests, and manually review upstream patches. Settle it by running a controlled test: apply Pret to our repo for two weeks, measure noise reduction vs. misfires, then decide.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: The real risk isn’t just upstream noise—it’s that auto-applying even our own whitespace patches could mask latent formatting bugs in tests or tooling. A better alternative: auto-apply only to files explicitly excluded from test coverage, where formatting drift won’t break anything. Settle it by running a dry-run on a non-critical module and measuring whether it catches real issues or just churn.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches only to files explicitly excluded from test coverage in our own codebase—trusting our safety net there, ignoring upstream entirely.

Result must deliver: a working patch pipeline that skips test-covered files, with a clear log of what changed and why. Owned by worker-1850.
